newsitem.title: New Zealand: Samurai rumours drive NZ yields down at close.
newsitem.headline: Samurai rumours drive NZ yields down at close.

text.p: * NZ yields finish lower across curve
* Rumours of samurai, eurokiwi boost sentiment
* 10-yr bonds rally after break below 8 pct
New Zealand debt markets rallied to an impressive finish on Wednesday after further rumours of samurai issuance, and expectations of another eurokiwi going through overnight.

The strength was seen right across the yield curve, with mid bonds rallying around 10 points and the 10-year maturities finishing 11 points lower at 7.91 percent. Dealers said the 11/06s were on a roll after breaking through the crucial eight percent level, and could push as low as 7.75 percent.
Money market dealers said trade slowed down after a strong open, until the bonds were paid after lunch and triggered further strength. Offshore buying in futures drove the physicals lower.
The front futures contracts ended 11 points stronger at 90.71 while 90-day bill rates closed down six to 9.86 percent.
Dealers said political uncertainty had been thrown to the wind, and the bills received an extra boost from gains in the Kiwi dollar during the day on the back of the samurai talk.

"It's about time really -- conditions were getting tighter and tighter with the bank bills holding their own and the currency going up, so maybe we'll come back to a bit more of a normal level now, " one said.
"Still, I think it's going to be range-bound up until the election.

"It could come a little bit stronger but I think you'll see sellers start coming in the 90-days at around 9.80-75 percent...and on the top end if it sells off above 9.95 you'd probably see a few happy to buy there."
New Zealand is just 10 days out from a general election on

NZ bonds outperformed other dollar bloc countries on Wednesday as talk surfaced around lunchtime of a samurai issuance, and another eurokiwi possibly going through overnight. Australian bonds pared their gains after opening at 2 1/2 year highs, as the hoped-for rate cut announcement from the RBA failed to eventuate.
